gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-noto-sans-kayah-li: Noto Sans Kayah Li keeps its capitals barely taller than its lowercase. Wallpoet sits above it as a loud display heading, its stencil-like gaps letting paper show through, while the body text stays smaller and quiet beneath.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-noto-sans-kharoshthi: Wallpoet is a bold display face whose lowercase rises high and whose bends run smooth and clear. Noto Sans Kharoshthi counters with curves that never close back on themselves and a dark, thick stripe of lowercase, which is the strongest thing about this pairing.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-noto-sans-khmer: Noto Sans Khmer has small letters that stand almost capital-sized. Against Wallpoet's commanding display lines, those generous chisel-notch openings give the pair its strongest quality: a loud heading sitting over a body that stays wide and readable.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Loud top, open bottom. Wallpoet's bold display letters, split by thin gaps where paper shows, sit over Noto Sans Khojki, whose wide exits and large e eyes let light pass through every line.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-noto-sans-khudawadi: Heavy display swagger meets a friendly sans-serif here, with Wallpoet commanding the heading and Noto Sans Khudawadi staying low in contrast between capitals and lowercase. And its rounds stay unlatched like an open hook, so a longer passage should move along without snagging.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-noto-sans-kr: Wallpoet takes the heading with bold, commanding display letters and a smooth path around every bend. Noto Sans KR follows with generous curve gaps and a big x-height under stubby ascenders and descenders, so the sturdy heading never crowds the text.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-noto-sans-lao: Stencil-style gaps cut right through Wallpoet's bold, commanding letters. Noto Sans Lao is the plain sans underneath, with a x-height pushed well above the usual and mouths that stay open, which is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-noto-sans-lao-looped: Noto Sans Lao Looped reads in solid blocks rather than skylines. A longer passage would feel dense and orderly, its bowls left unfinished on one side, while Wallpoet shouts above as a bold display heading.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-noto-sans-lepcha: Noto Sans Lepcha reads as a plain sans with wide curve openings and lowercase carrying the stature of cast iron capitals. Beside Wallpoet's bold, commanding display lines, that sturdy body is the strongest quality in the pair.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Noto Sans Limbu reads with tall-bodied small letters and curves that look like they are gaping. And Wallpoet, bold and commanding with gaps where paper shows through, gives the pair its strongest quality: a heading that is loud over an open sans.
